meaning: Number of family heads among the warriors under King Uzziah; otherwise without prominent symbolic meaning
description: The number 2600 appears in 2 Chronicles 26:12, where it indicates the total number of family heads among the brave warriors under King Uzziah (Azariah) of Judah. These 2600 family heads led a military force of 307,500 men, which underscores Uzziah's military power and God's blessing over his reign – during the period when he was faithful to the Lord. Beyond this specific occurrence, the number 2600 has no well-established symbolic meaning in biblical or Jewish tradition, unlike numbers such as 7, 12, 40, and 613 which carry deep theological symbolism.

versions.meaning: The number 2600 has no well-established or prominent symbolic significance in biblical or Jewish tradition.
versions.description: The number 2600 does not appear as a symbolically important number in the Bible or in central Jewish texts. While certain numbers such as 7, 12, 40, and 613 carry deep symbolic and theological meaning in these traditions, there is no recognized tradition that attributes special symbolism to the number 2600. It may be noted, however, that some have attempted to link it to chronological calculations, such as the period from creation to certain biblical events, but this is not widely accepted as symbolically significant.

footnotes.text: King Uzziah (also called Azariah) reigned over Judah for 52 years and was one of the longest-reigning kings. His strength and success are attributed to his faithfulness to God, but his downfall came when he arrogantly entered the temple to burn incense—an act reserved for priests (2 Chron. 26:16–21).

Some chronologists have attempted to link the number 2600 to time calculations from creation to various biblical events, but such calculations vary significantly among different traditions and are not widely accepted.
